payload.excerpt: How to choose a wedding RSVP website for a destination wedding: the kinds of RSVP website compared, what to check before you pay for an upgrade, what to ask guests, QR codes on invitations and keeping guest details private.
key_takeaways: Choose the kind of RSVP website by what your weekend needs, such as separate replies for each event and travel questions, rather than by the look of the template.
Before paying for an upgrade, check guest and event limits, custom questions, exports, password protection and whether guests see the tool's branding or ads.
Print the RSVP web address beside any QR code and test-scan the printed proof before the full print run.
Ask guests only for the details your planning needs, keep the list private and delete what you no longer need after the wedding.

faq.q: Which type of wedding RSVP website suits a destination wedding?
faq.a: One that handles several events in one reply and lets you add travel and accommodation questions. An all-in-one wedding website or a planning app with RSVP can both do this.

faq.q: Can you collect wedding RSVPs online without paying?
faq.a: Yes, on a no-cost tier. Check guest and event limits, custom questions, export, branding and ads before you commit.

faq.q: Can guests RSVP without creating an account?
faq.a: It depends on the tool, so check before you choose: a sign-up step can make guests put the reply off.

faq.q: Can one RSVP website handle several wedding events?
faq.a: Some can, with a separate yes or no for each event in a single reply. Test it as a guest before you send.

faq.q: How do QR code RSVPs work on a printed invitation?
faq.a: The code opens your RSVP page on the guest's phone. Print the web address beside it, create the code with a trusted tool and test-scan the proof before printing.

faq.q: Is it okay for wedding guests to RSVP online?
faq.a: Yes, as long as there is a gentle alternative. For older relatives, or anyone who would rather not reply online, offer a phone number or email and add their answers yourself.
